variations: Seated or senior version: skip the trot, set Sniff on a rug runner beside the mat, and make Event 2 a slow stroll of a few steps.
Puppy version: Sniff and Snooze only, on a soft mat with a short, quiet event two.
Two-dog home: run each dog alone with the other behind a closed door, and give each their own mat and water in separate rooms for the Snooze.

Siesta edition: before the Snooze, let your dog watch you tuck a favorite toy (or a piece of today's ration) into a low basket beside the mat. After they wake on their own, stay still and see whether they head for it. Finding it, ignoring it or going back to sleep all count; if they seem done, just set it beside them.
supplies: A mat, folded blanket or towel
A scarf or towel for the start ribbon
A little of today's regular food
optionalSupplies: A tea or glass of water for your own toast
A phone for the podium photo
substitutes: No mat? Use a folded duvet or the dog's own bed.
No runner? A yoga mat or a row of bath mats with a non-slip backing.
title: The Napathlon
clue: Three events, one medal, and the winner is whoever stops first.
reveal: A home triathlon for your dog: Sniff, Stroll, Snooze. Each event is easy and optional, the commentary is yours, and the gold medal always goes to the nap.
objective: Run three gentle events in order (nose, legs, rest) and award the gold medal to the quiet one.
instructions: Build the arena: a hallway or yard strip about six steps long with grippy footing (a runner, yoga mat or dry grass; not bare wood, tile or wet decking). Clear it, close doors, and lay a scarf flat on the floor as the start ribbon. Put the nap mat and a water bowl at the far end.
Opening ceremony: sit down, read the program in a hushed commentator voice, and let your dog wander in. They can watch from anywhere; the ceremony has no audience requirement.
Event 1, Sniff: drop six to eight pieces of today's ration along the runway edge, spaced a few steps apart. Let your dog take the trail at their own speed and skip pieces if they like.

Event 2, Stroll: sit by the mat at the far end, relaxed and facing slightly away. If your dog ambles, trots or bounds over, that is the event. One or two goes at most. Never chase, call repeatedly or run toward them.

Event 3, Snooze: dim the lights, leave the water bowl by the mat, stop talking and sit a little distance away. The judge scores one thing only: how soon the head goes down, a sigh happens or the eyes soften.
Podium: whenever the dog settles, rest a calm hand flat on the mat edge for a moment as the medal, or simply raise your water glass in silence. Then leave them be until they stir.
twist: The judge has one rule: you only win this triathlon by stopping.
completion: Your dog has had at least one event they chose, and you have awarded the medal, even if the Snooze was a lie-down and a sniff.
photoIdea: A side-on photo of your dog on the mat after the podium, with the start ribbon scarf in the background.
memoryPrompt: Which event did your dog choose to go back to, and how long did the gold medal take?
dietNotes: Use part of today's normal ration and count it in. Ask your vet if your dog has dietary restrictions, allergies or health conditions.
safety: Use a non-slip surface for the middle event, and skip it if your dog slips.
Never chase or call a dog over and over: one or two invitations is plenty.
Use only part of today's normal food, never chocolate, grapes, raisins or xylitol.
Skip the Siesta edition if your dog guards toys or food, and never leave anything out for pets to compete over.
